{{move|Gracidea Garden}} {{AnimeLocationInfobox |name=Gracidea |characters=グラシデア |japanese=Gracidea |image=Gracidea anime.png |imagesize=250px |region=Sinnoh |epicode=M11 |episode=Giratina and the Sky Warrior }} '''Gracidea''' (Japanese: '''グラシデア''' ''Gracidea'') is a vast area located in [[Sinnoh]]. It is near the top of a mountain. {{OBP|Shaymin|M11}}, along with others of its species, lives here. If a Shaymin comes in contact with [[Gracidea|one of the flowers found in this place]], it will immediately change Forme. In the English dub, the Gracidea garden was also referred to as the "flower garden". ==History== [[File:Shaymin Gracidea overhead.png|thumb|left|220px|Aerial view of Gracidea]] Gracidea was featured in ''[[M11|Giratina and the Sky Warrior]]''. It is located at the base of a glacier. Shaymin was in a rush to get there in time for "flower bearing," a ritual where many Shaymin gather, transform into Sky Forme, and fly away to start a new Gracidea garden in a faraway place. The place was threatened with destruction when [[Zero]]'s actions in the [[Reverse World]] caused the glacier to start moving. A {{p|Regigigas}}, who inhabited a temple in the mountains near the garden, awoke just in time to help stop the impending disaster. [[File:Shaymin Gracidea.png|thumb|250px|Several Shaymin in Gracidea]] {{left clear}} ==Trivia== * Gracidea did not appear in {{game2|Diamond|Pearl|Platinum}}, but the [[Flower Paradise]] can be considered its counterpart, as it is covered in flowers and Shaymin can be found there. However, the [[Gracidea]] flower itself is not found there; instead, it is found in [[Floaroma Town]]. ===Origin=== {{main|Pokémon world in relation to the real world#In the movies|Pokémon world in relation to the real world → In the movies}} The area surrounding Gracidea is modeled after {{wp|Jostedal Glacier}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 3: The Experience of "Climbing a Glacier!" - Part 1) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20071210224443/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/03.html archived]) (Japanese) and {{wp|Sognefjord}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 2: Journey through the Fjord) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20071212204945/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/02.html archived]) (Japanese) in {{wp|Norway}}.
